name: Contract administration and obligation management
one_line: Running a contract AFTER it is signed: the register that lists what is in force, the obligations and service levels it created, the notice and renewal dates that must be diarised, the variations and change orders that amend it, the performance reports that test it, and the correspondence that manages it to expiry or termination. The anchor is a LIVE OBLIGATION and its calendar — not the negotiation that produced the instrument and not the instrument itself. Absorbs the legacy row ops.contract-administration. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The business_operations schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row's sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a register structure: a table whose columns include a counterparty, a contract reference, a start date, an end or expiry date, a notice date or notice period, a value, and an internal owner — one row per agreement. The notice-date column is the single most characteristic signal in this row and it appears in no other family's tables. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
an obligation-tracker structure: obligations extracted from an instrument into rows, each with a clause reference, a responsible party, a frequency, and a due or review date.

a notice structure: a formal letter carrying a labelled clause reference, an effective date, a delivery method, and a served-on or acknowledged-by block — renewal, non-renewal, termination, breach, price review, or assignment.
a variation structure: a change order, amendment, or deed of variation naming a parent agreement by reference and date, with a numbered amendment sequence and its own execution block.
a service-level or performance structure: a periodic report of measured performance against defined targets with a credit, remedy, or escalation column referring back to a schedule.

a contract summary or abstract: a one-page precis carrying labelled slots for parties, term, value, notice, governing law and key obligations — produced BY the administration function and by nothing else.

a recurring calendar entry or reminder whose labelled SUMMARY names a contract reference and a notice or renewal event. “Calendar formats such as ICS should yield event title, start and end time, location, organizer, attendees, and recurrence metadata.” The CONTENT is what fires; source_type = calendar contributes only as a file-kind signal.
parent-folder context naming a counterparty, a contract reference, or a renewal year, treated as a clue once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this world is commercially confidential and often confidential to a THIRD party, so any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

the central determination for this row: separating the INSTRUMENT from its ADMINISTRATION. A signed agreement is a legal record; the register entry, the diary date and the renewal letter that run it are this row. Both are usually in one folder, and a single executed PDF with a manuscript renewal note on the cover is genuinely both.

separating the BUYING side from the SELLING side of the same agreement. A supplier contract and a customer contract are the same document filed by two parties, and the parties block states two names in two roles without saying which side the filesystem belongs to. This is the third role the canonical field list has no key for.

separating a real executed agreement from a template, a precedent, a draft under negotiation, and a downloaded model form — a redline is a negotiation artifact, not an administration one. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
unlabelled contract correspondence: a chasing email about an unnamed renewal, a note about a price increase, a dispute opener with no reference.

a purpose-coherent contract file whose members are individually unremarkable — an executed PDF, a register extract, two amendments, an SLA report and a calendar reminder. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: an executed agreement alone. A signature block and numbered clauses are the legal family's shape, and the tempting false file for this row is precisely a signed contract with no administration around it.
contract vocabulary alone — agreement, term, renewal, notice, counterparty, SLA. Employment contracts, tenancy agreements, personal loan agreements and published model forms are all dense in it.

a counterparty name alone, which is worse than 00's university case because a company name in a parties block is present in exactly two roles at once and the document does not say which is the holder's.
a date-shaped token read as a renewal or notice date. Contracts are dense in dates — execution, commencement, effective, review, invoice — and only a labelled slot distinguishes them.

a company, charity, or regulator gazetteer hit alone. 00 states the ambiguity for a university — “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — and a company name is worse, appearing as employer, customer, supplier, competitor, regulator, and as the letterhead of a document that is merely ABOUT the holder. Stated as inference; 00 writes that sentence about a university, not a company.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session that emptied a document-management system or a mail thread's attachments at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — a corporate template stamps the same entity on every blank form it ever generated.
a bare 4-digit number read as a fiscal year, an entity number, a contract number, or a document version.

work_types: executed agreement or counterpart (as an administered item)
notice letter (renewal, non-renewal, termination, breach, price review)
insurance or warranty evidence held under a contract
grouping_reasons: one contract lifecycle: the instrument, its amendments, the register entry, the notices, the performance reports and the renewal papers — the clearest group in this family and the one users most expect.

one counterparty across several agreements over time — a real reason to group, and the one most likely to tempt a counterparty label onto a bare invoice or reminder, which is exactly what must not happen. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”

one renewal event: the diary entry, the internal recommendation, the notice and the acknowledgement — purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one register as it is re-exported over time, joined by the universal duplicate_family and version_family facts rather than by any business fact.
no group at all is a valid outcome: an isolated notice letter with no reference is an ordinary standalone record.
and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two counterparties' files in one folder do not merge.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry's schema declares, and business_operations declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row's open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the counterparty or the contract itself, then the agreement or contract reference where one counterparty has several, then the document function (instrument / variation / notice / performance), with the renewal period only where the corpus really cycles annually. An amendment is unintelligible above its parent agreement, which is 00's own reason for putting a course above a homework number. Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The load-bearing collision on this row. A signed agreement is the legal family's instrument and this row's administered item, and a single executed PDF is both. The discriminating evidence: an execution block, defined terms and a governing-law clause support the instrument; a register row, a notice date, an obligation tracker, or a renewal letter support this row. Because legal is a field-less safety placeholder, where both fire the protective ordering runs first. Provenance: inference.

Redlines, issues lists and negotiation correspondence look like administration correspondence. The discriminating evidence: tracked changes, a comparison document, a negotiation issues list, or a matter identifier and an engagement framing support the practitioner row; a live post-signature obligation, a register and a diary date support this row. Provenance: inference.

Procurement produces the contract this row then runs, and the boundary is the signature. The discriminating evidence: a requirement, a tender, an evaluation matrix or an award letter supports procurement; anything dated after execution — the register entry, the variation, the renewal — supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Supplier performance reviews and supplier risk records overlap the SLA reports here almost completely. The discriminating evidence: a contractual clause reference, a service credit, or a notice consequence supports this row; a relationship-level scorecard, an onboarding record, or a supplier risk assessment with no clause anchor supports vendor management. The pair is thin and R1c should confirm both rows survive. Provenance: inference.

A renewal is administered on one side and sold on the other, from the same date and often the same spreadsheet. The discriminating evidence: a notice clause, a register entry and a formal letter support this row; an account plan, a usage or adoption record and a renewal PROPOSAL support the account row. Provenance: inference.

Subcontract administration — variations, payment notices, delay claims — is this row's shape in a sector that has its own statutory notice regime. The discriminating evidence: a site, a works package, a valuation number, or a statutory payment-notice reference supports the construction row; a general commercial register and notice calendar supports this row. Provenance: inference.

An authority's contract management and a supplier's copy of the same agreement are identical documents. The discriminating evidence is which side the holder is on: a statutory procurement regime, a published award notice, or a contracting-authority framing supports the government row; a supplier's or buyer's own private register supports this row. Provenance: inference.

A statement of work is the individual's engagement record and the delivering organisation's contract record at once. The discriminating evidence: a document held to evidence the holder's own engagement, deliverables and fees supports the career row; the register, notice calendar and obligation tracker that run it as one of many support this row. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: Executed agreements, notices and registers are commercially confidential and routinely name individuals as signatories or contacts, so this is the primary protective home. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The honest outcome for a register, a report, or a chasing note whose contract and side are unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The home for a standalone notice, acknowledgement or certificate with no contract file around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

Isolated transactional members — a purchase order, a call-off confirmation, a supplier invoice with no register around it. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

Model forms, NDA templates and precedent agreements are the tempting false files of this row. “Reference Clips may live under Personal/Reference Clips and hold saved visual inspiration, product references, quotes, recipes, short article captures, code snippets, or other material that is useful for later retrieval but does not belong to a current project.”

Password-protected contract exports and signing-platform bundles are ordinary here. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: Contracts are confidential by their own terms — most contain a clause saying so — and 00's corpus sentence names the category directly: the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”, and an agreement is a legal record. Beyond that, and as inference rather than a design claim, this row is unusual in that the exposed party is normally NOT the user: a counterparty's pricing, an employee named as a signatory, a customer's terms. They cannot consent to what the product does with the file, which argues for the cautious setting. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two. (1) The BUYING-versus-SELLING role has no canonical key. 00's role_split pair is `our_firm` / `client`, which covers the professional-services reading; the supplier role in a buy-side register is a third role with no key, and this row is where that hole is most visible. A `supplier` key is worth proposing at R1c, and this row deliberately does NOT mint one. (2) Whether this row and business_operations.vendor-management are genuinely two situations. Their detection signals overlap more than any other pair in the family, and the honest reading is that this row is contract-anchored and that one is relationship-anchored — defensible, but thin enough that R1c should confirm rather than inherit it.
